newsitem.title: POLAND: Poland issues finding on post-war Swiss accounts.
newsitem.headline: Poland issues finding on post-war Swiss accounts.

text.p: Money from Swiss bank accounts belonging to Polish Jews who died in the Holocaust was not paid as compensation to Swiss citizens whose assets were seized by the communists after World War Two, PAP news agency said on Tuesday.
The agency quoted the Warsaw Foreign Ministry as saying a special cross-ministry committee had reached the initial finding after probing 1949 agreements between Warsaw and Switzerland.

Switzerland stands accused by Senator Alfonse D'Amato, chairman of the powerful U.S. Senate Banking Committee, of agreeing to give money to Poland from unclaimed bank accounts of Polish citizens, as part of an accord on compensating Swiss nationals whose assets had been seized in communist Poland.
Many of these citizens were Jews murdered during the war, when Nazi German invaders killed most of Poland's 3.5 million Jews.
"Compensation for Swiss properties nationalised in Poland were not paid with money from so-called 'dead accounts' in Swiss banks," PAP reported the Polish committee as saying.
However, the committee found the 1949 agreements with Switzerland contained "significant legal shortcomings," it quoted Foreign Ministry spokesman Pawel Dobrowolski as saying.
He said, however, that Poland did not have the names of its citizens who had opened accounts in Switzerland before the war.

Switzerland has accused D'Amato, who is backed by Jewish groups demanding compensation, of sensationalising isolated facts in his accusation that the Swiss profited from Germany's murder of Jews. It has promised to unearth the full facts.

Last month the Warsaw Foreign Ministry said Poland and Switzerland had signed agreements on June 25, 1949, on commodities exchanges -- largely sales of Polish coal -- and on compensating Swiss citizens, both with confidential protocols.
The compensation accord had a protocol and exchange of letters on unclaimed accounts of Poles in Swiss institutions.

A common payments mechanism, an account in Switzerland belonging to the National Bank of Poland (NBP), was set up and from it money from Polish exports was distributed to meet claims by Swiss citizens.

But at the same time money from Polish accounts in Swiss banks was flowing the other way into the same account, it said after first checks on the past deals clinched by Poland's former communist rulers, who were toppled from power in 1989.
PAP said on Tuesday that the committee would this month submit a final report to the Foreign Ministry on the dormant accounts and on the payments mechanism.
